590051|2026-03.headline: Saksoft Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% YoY to INR 249 crore, with FY26 crossing INR 1,000 crore; management says pipeline is at a record ~USD 25 million.
590051|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR 249 crore, up roughly 4% YoY and down about 0.8% QoQ, while EBITDA grew 24% YoY to INR 45 crore at an 18.19% margin. FY26 revenue was about INR 1,007 crore (up ~14%), EBITDA INR 187 crore (18.57% margin) and net profit INR 133 crore (up 23%). Management said decision-making by customers has slowed amid AI-related uncertainty, though the pipeline has grown sharply, and it guided to 30% growth as a stretch target with 14-15% as the floor. Management was clear that the AI theme is pervasive, and it expects some margin compression near term from AI-driven renewal price cuts.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue)
segments.commentary: Americas ~50%, Europe 29%, Asia Pacific and other regions 21%.

segments.name: Vertical (FY26 revenue)
segments.commentary: Emerging Verticals 47% (high-tech and telecom), Banking & Financial Services ~31%, Logistics 14%, Commerce 8%.

segments.name: Delivery mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Onsite 44%, offshore 56%. Technical headcount 2,277 of 2,494 total at quarter end; utilization 83% for FY26 (excluding trainees).

segments.name: Customers
segments.commentary: Around 16 customers at USD 1 million+ revenue. Top 10 clients ~58% of revenue (per analyst question); top 20 clients ~70% of revenue (per management).

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to 30% growth in FY27 but said it is a 'tough call'; it expects 14-15% as the bare minimum and would put more money on 14-15%.
EBITDA margin: management aims to maintain the 17-18% range, but flagged a 'little bit of a dip' from AI investment and AI-driven price cuts at contract renewal.
Management expects growth to pick up as decision-making improves, targeting Q1 and Q2 FY27 for that pick-up.
Target of USD 500 million revenue by 2030; management says no significant capex is needed, funded by internal cash generation.
No guidance given on bottom-line margin for next year.
Headcount growth expected to be less than proportional to revenue growth; management sees utilization capped at about 85% due to the bench needed for agents and projects.
capex_capacity: Management says no significant capex is needed to reach USD 500 million by 2030; investment is in people and technology, funded by cash generation.
Continued investment in AI capabilities, accelerators and training of developers, project managers and leads on multiple LLMs.
Front-end investment: Chief Growth Officer in the US in place for about 9-10 months; Chief Growth Officer for UK and Europe joining end of June 2026.
Utilization (excluding trainees) of 83% for FY26; management sees 85% as the practical ceiling.
Technical employees fell about 4.5% in FY26 and total headcount about 5%, per analyst figures.
demand_pricing: Pipeline at about USD 25 million, the highest ever, versus about USD 5 million six months earlier; management credits a new US Chief Growth Officer and concerted sales effort.
Decision-making is slower; in Q3 two large customers deferred spending; in Q4 one resumed and the other is still deferring.
95-98% of growth and pipeline is from existing customers; management targets wallet share in top 20 accounts and says they could alone reach USD 500 million.
Vendor consolidation offers of 25-30% cost reduction are being used to win larger deals; Commerce is the smallest pipeline vertical.
Outcome-based billing is about 10% of revenue; the rest is time and material. Management is pushing outcome-based models and expects AI to reshape team composition.
Of FY26 growth of ~14%, management said ~3 points were currency (rupee depreciation); the rest came from volume growth at existing clients, not price.
Management expects some renewal price compression as customers seek AI productivity gains, with cannibalisation within contracts but overall spend expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Has sequential growth picked up back to the 3.5-4% QoQ range after two flattish quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is picking up but customer decisions are deferred due to AI noise; it expects Q1 and Q2 FY27 to see decisions pick up, with a record pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Would acquisitions be possible given the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions would be funded from internal accruals with maybe some borrowing; the maximum size considered is a target with top line of INR 100 crore. Nothing is imminent this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can 17-18% EBITDA margins be sustained in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will try to maintain them but expects a possible dip from AI investment and renewal price cuts; it sees no major concern.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a headcount decline and utilization rise toward 90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilization is capped at about 85% (agents may be counted in utilization); headcount will not scale linearly with revenue if AI adoption happens.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% growth target realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30% is a stretch; 14-15% is the bare minimum, and it would expect around 15% even if the rupee appreciates somewhat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall to about INR 12 crore in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the prior-year figure included a bad-debt provision for a US customer that went bust; no significant provisions were made in FY26, and the current run-rate should broadly continue.

risks_watch: Customer decision-making delays tied to AI uncertainty could keep sequential growth flat; watch Q1 and Q2 FY27 conversion of the USD 25 million pipeline.
Client concentration: top 10 clients ~58% of revenue, top 20 ~70%; loss of a large account would hit growth.
Margin pressure from AI-driven price cuts at renewal and from investment; management said AI costs could exceed human costs and remains an open variable.
Rupee depreciation contributed ~3 points of FY26 growth; a stronger rupee would reduce reported growth.

Structural risks flagged in Q&A: GCC insourcing (management says relevant mainly for large enterprises), cannibalisation of contracts, and the shift from time and material to outcome-based pricing (~10% today).
Ask on FY26 other expenses: the low Q4 level is partly due to the absence of the prior-year bad-debt provision, so the run-rate should be verified next quarter.
590051|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on pipeline strength and long-term AI positioning, but cautious on near-term growth, citing deferred customer decisions and AI-related uncertainty. Management openly called 30% growth a stretch and steered expectations to 14-15%. It was evasive on AI revenue disclosure and declined to give margin guidance.
key_quotes: Our pipeline is really strong. I would say it's probably the strongest it's ever been in the last in the history of the company.
We are shooting for 30% growth. Now will 30% happen? It' s going to be a tough call.
Our top 20 customers give us about 70% of our revenue, okay?
So even if we were to get no new logo, we could achieve that $500 million just by increasing wallet share in these 20 accounts.

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and bank balance (31 Mar 2026)

financial_highlights.value: INR 0.55 per share (55% of face value INR 1); total 100% for the year

rows.why: Management aims to hold the 17-18% EBITDA margin (FY26 18.57%) but flagged a 'little bit of a dip' from AI investment and renewal price cuts, so compression is more likely than expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says no significant capex is needed to reach USD 500 million by 2030 and utilisation (83% FY26) is capped at about 85%, so no new capacity is signalled; growth is to come from headcount-light delivery.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pipeline is at about USD 25 million versus about USD 5 million six months earlier, 95-98% from existing clients, and FY26 growth of ~14% was volume-led; management targets 14-15% as the floor, with 30% as a stretch.

rows.why: Management says no significant capex is needed and utilisation is 83% with a practical ceiling of 85%, so a capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management calls 30% a stretch and 14-15% the floor; upside depends on Q1-Q2 FY27 conversion of the USD 25 million pipeline, which is still being deferred by some customers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Two large customers deferred spending in Q3 and one was still deferring in Q4, and AI renewal price cuts could pull growth toward the 14-15% floor or below it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Product or service launches were not discussed; AI investment is in people, accelerators and training rather than named offerings.

rows.label: Pipeline conversion of USD 25 million
rows.why: Pipeline rose from about USD 5 million six months earlier to about USD 25 million, but one of two deferring customers was still deferring in Q4, so conversion depends on decisions resuming.

rows.label: AI-driven renewal price cuts
rows.why: Management expects some renewal price compression as customers seek AI productivity gains, with vendor consolidation offers of 25-30% cost reduction being used to win larger deals.

rows.why: Q4 other expenses fell to about INR 12 crore because the prior-year bad-debt provision was absent; the run-rate needs verification next quarter and a recurrence would weigh on margin.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record pipeline and AI positioning but cautious on near-term growth, calling 30% a stretch and steering to 14-15%; analysts pressed on utilisation, headcount, margin sustainability and the other-expense run-rate.

590051|2026-06.headline: Saksoft Q1 FY27 revenue flat at about INR 249 crore, EBITDA INR 45 crore (18.26% margin); FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore held.
590051|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was about INR 249 crore, broadly flat year on year, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (down 1% YoY) and PAT of about INR 29 crore (11.78% margin). Management said demand softness that began in Q3 FY26 continued, with top clients delaying renewals and decisions. Pipeline is stated to be far larger than the USD 25 million cited last quarter, now about USD 28 million, but conversion is slow. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore (about 25% growth on FY26's INR 1,007 crore) while saying Q2 looks muted and growth is expected in H2.

financial_highlights.change: flat, per management, as revenue is flat
headcount declining over last two quarters per analyst
management target at least 65% in 2-3 years

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Americas 52% of revenue, Europe 27%, Asia Pacific and other 21%.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Emerging verticals 45%, BFSI about 30%, transportation and logistics about 16%, digital commerce 9%. Management expects growth in emerging verticals first, then BFSI and logistics; digital commerce sees the most headwinds. BFSI revenue flat in absolute terms Q4 to Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore maintained; management will restate at end of Q2 if needed.
Next quarter (Q2 FY27) expected to remain muted; management hopeful of growth in H2 FY27.
Management expects headcount to flatten or decline while revenue grows, driven by AI productivity and shift to outcome-based and managed services.
Management expects employee and resource costs as a percentage of revenue to decline over time; about 77% of costs are employee plus contractor costs, with appraisals impacting next quarter.
Management claims AI gives 30-50% efficiency in product engineering and 20-30% in managed services, per management rule of thumb.
Long-term target of INR 500 million (analyst cited FY30) was referenced but management focused on FY27 only.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning details were discussed.
Headcount reduction attributed to AI-driven engineering productivity, AI agents replacing recruitment and invoicing/payables roles, and move away from headcount-linked contracts.
demand_pricing: Management says pipeline is at a record level, now about USD 28 million versus USD 25 million last quarter, with quality improved by a shift to bigger managed-services and outcome-based deals.
Decision-making is delayed; top clients face near-term pressures. Management says nothing is normalizing, though it expects recovery in medium term.
Company deliberately avoids headcount/body-shop deals, which is causing near-term revenue pain.
Company is exiting tail accounts without potential to scale; exact number of accounts let go to be sent later.
Competition has increased as larger IT players bid for smaller deals, but management says mid-sized firms are gaining access to bigger RFPs because of AI.
New logo added in first month by new Chief Growth Officer for Europe: a logistics/airline company that is a major supplier to Amazon.
AI: company does not track AI revenue separately; management says all projects contain AI components and none are pilots.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline now versus last quarter, and when will conversion and growth show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pipeline is about USD 28 million versus USD 25 million last quarter, with better quality. Next quarter looks muted, with growth hoped for in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR 1,200-1,250 crore, about 25% growth on INR 1,007 crore in FY26, and will restate at end of Q2 if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals drive growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Emerging verticals first, then BFSI and logistics. Digital commerce has the most headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost falling and what will new senior hires add?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount falls from AI productivity, AI agents in support functions, and a shift to outcome-based deals. Two senior hires were funded by repurposing costs of founders who exited after earnouts, so management does not expect employee cost to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company letting go of tail clients, and how is client concentration changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is exiting accounts without scale potential. Top 10 concentration fell from 58% to 56%, and it has no target to reduce it further.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue comes from AI and what is the AI deal-size trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not break out AI revenue. It said every project includes AI, and pure AI work is limited to AI co-innovation labs.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from the US and how will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: US share is 52% (management corrected from 55%), with a target of at least 65% in two to three years.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted, and FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore requires a sharp H2 recovery from a flat H1.
Deal conversion is slow as the shift to larger outcome-based deals lengthens decision cycles.
Digital commerce faces the most headwinds, and BFSI revenue is flat QoQ.
Management did not quantify the number of accounts exited; it promised to send figures later. Pipeline figure of USD 28 million is also to be confirmed in writing.
Long-term INR 500 million target (FY30) was raised by an analyst but not addressed by management.
Competition from larger IT players moving down into smaller deals.
Appraisals next quarter could push up employee costs.
590051|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term demand and conversion, with management openly saying Q2 will be muted and that they do not expect improvement soon. It is more confident on the medium-term pipeline, AI productivity and the move to managed services, but it gave few hard numbers beyond the FY27 guidance it reiterated.
key_quotes: Decision making is getting delayed unfortunately, and we are pushing as hard as we can, but there is a limit to how much you can fight the industry
Numbers will come, growth will come, it won't happen overnight.
Nothing is pilot, everything is in production.

rows.why: EBITDA margin held at 18.26% with headcount falling and management expecting employee and resource costs as a share of revenue to decline over time, but appraisals next quarter could push costs up.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue was flat YoY at about INR 249 crore and Q2 is guided muted, so growth depends on a sharp H2 recovery from the USD 28 million pipeline (up from USD 25 million) converting.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 83% but management discussed no capex and is shifting to AI productivity and headcount reduction, not new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore (about 25% growth) was only held, and H1 is flat, so an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Flat H1 against a guide needing about 25% growth means a sharp H2 recovery is required, and management said it will restate at end of Q2 if needed.

rows.label: Pipeline rise to USD 28 million with slow conversion
rows.why: Pipeline rose from USD 25 million to about USD 28 million, but management says conversion is slow and decisions are delayed, with growth expected in H2.

rows.label: US share target of at least 65% from 52%
rows.why: US share is 52% of revenue today against a stated target of at least 65% in 2-3 years, but no interim numbers were given.

rows.label: Headcount reduction from AI productivity
rows.why: Management expects headcount to flatten or decline while revenue grows, with 2,434 employees today and headcount already falling over the last two quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term pipeline, AI productivity and the shift to managed services, but cautious on near-term demand, saying Q2 will be muted. Analysts pushed on the FY27 guidance, the pipeline conversion and the headcount decline.

590051|2026-09.headline: Saksoft Q2 FY27 revenue flat QoQ at about INR249 crores; PAT up 10% QoQ to INR32 crores on a 12.92% margin.
590051|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR249 crores, broadly flat QoQ, while EBITDA fell 4% QoQ to about INR44 crores with margin down 66 bps to 17.6%. PAT rose 10% QoQ to about INR32 crores. H1 FY27 operating income was INR497 crores (down 2% YoY), with EBITDA down 8% YoY to INR89 crores. Management attributed flat revenue to AI-driven efficiency cannibalisation, client insourcing and slow US pipeline conversion, and said H2 will be better than H1 without quantifying it.

qa_highlights.question: How will the USD500 million revenue target by 2030 be funded and split between organic and inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the target mammoth but said it is confident of getting close to it, if not reaching it. It is pursuing M&A, partner-led pull (ServiceNow, Salesforce) and campaigns. M&A will be funded from internal cash and limited debt, with no equity dilution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,200 crore FY27 guidance still valid, implying about 40% growth in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working on non-linear options that could significantly lift revenue, called it a tough ask, and said investments come before results. Another analyst cited INR1,250 crores; management said a number close enough is possible if options work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook if nothing non-linear materialises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will be better than H1 and suggested around INR1,100 crores. It said Q3 was about half complete with good visibility.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the retail weakness and the loss in some accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no client was lost, but some projects with existing customers ended, and this should pick up.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins return to 19-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Not in the next two quarters, given sales and leadership investment and the shift to outcome-based work. Management said it is definitely possible within 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI deflation being offset by pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no rate cuts, only revenue cuts from efficiency. Price increases offset only part of the loss, so short-term revenue falls before clients return with more work.

risks_watch: Revenue cannibalisation from AI-led efficiency, with the company smaller than Tier 1 and Tier 2 peers that can offset it across large contracts.

590073|2026-09.headline: Wheels India Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 36% to INR1,598 crores and net profit to INR53.4 crores, with EBITDA margin at about 8%.
590073|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue grew 36% YoY to INR1,598 crores from INR1,179 crores, and net profit rose to INR53.4 crores from INR27.8 crores. Growth came mainly from earthmover wheels (largely exported), air suspension and the domestic auto segment, while the industrial segment grew more slowly. EBITDA was about 8% and PBT about 4%, and management said the debt repayment done in the last days of the quarter meant no interest benefit was captured yet. Management flagged inflation, a high GST 2.0 base from H2 FY26 that may slow growth from Q3, and a weak monsoon affecting tractor demand in some states.

segments.name: Auto (car, truck, tractor, earthmover wheels, air suspension)
segments.commentary: Grew almost 40% YoY, driven mainly by earthmover wheels and air suspension, with regular wheels also contributing. Air suspension volume grew about 50% YoY.

segments.name: Industrial (windmill, hydraulics, construction fabrication, machining)
segments.commentary: Growth was muted. Construction fabrication was slow, and windmill was seasonally slow with recovery expected from Q3. Management guided for industrial to turn profitable by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Cast aluminium (LPDC) wheels
segments.commentary: Capacity is 80,000 wheels/month, rising to 130,000 by end-March 2027. Breakeven of about 40,000/month reached, with PBT positive expected from December. Management targets 10-15% share of passenger car aluminium wheels within about a year.

segments.name: Windmill machining
segments.commentary: Job-work business with a double-digit EBITDA margin, roughly INR10 crores/month, expected to roughly double over two years as the casting partner scales from 3,500 to 5,000 tonnes/month.

segments.name: Hydraulic cylinders
segments.commentary: Low single-digit margin today. Scale-up expected from Q4 FY27 after layout changes, with supplies to international partners planned from January.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit EBITDA margin targeted in about two years; management said it would reach 10-12% EBITDA at 100,000 aluminium wheels/month, expected around Q1 FY28.
Price pass-through claims for raw materials and fuel (West Asia crisis) are in progress; closure expected by Q3, with margin upside from Q3 as management described it.
Capex guided at INR400-450 crores for FY27: about INR200 crores for aluminium wheels, about INR100 crores for industrial, and INR100-150 crores for conventional steel wheels.
Growth expected to slow from Q3 FY27 due to the high GST 2.0 base; visibility beyond Q3 is limited, per management.
Working capital is not expected to rise further at current activity levels, so accruals over the next two quarters will fund capex; undrawn loan lines remain available.
capex_capacity: Cast aluminium wheels: capacity 80,000/month now, 130,000/month by end-March 2027, with a 170,000 phase also referenced; roughly INR200 crores for adding about 90,000/month at an existing site. Next-phase capex already being planned.
Air suspension volumes growing about 50% YoY; management plans further capacity additions at its own and supplier facilities.
Hydraulic cylinders: layout changes under way, output step-up from January.
Windmill machining: casting partner expanding from 3,500 to 5,000 tonnes/month from December-January, with a further step to 6,500 tonnes/month in 12-18 months.
Bosch JV (electronic air suspension for commercial vehicles, about INR100 crores investment, Wheels India 20% stake) awaiting European competition clearance.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strong across segments, but expects growth to slow from Q3 due to the GST 2.0 base effect and flagged inflation concerns.
Tractor demand grew strongly in H1, but poor monsoon in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh may moderate it from Q4; north India remains firm. Globally the tractor cycle is down.
Aluminium wheel economics: average realisation about INR5,000/wheel; management said breakeven is about 40,000/month.
Passenger car steel wheels: about 35% share (management says the 40% aluminium segment is included in that base). Aluminium wheel share is in the low single digits, with a 10-15% target.
US business grew 50% in H1, driven by earthmover and windmill products. Management said order visibility is monthly customer schedules, not a formal order book.
Management said it will not enter truck air suspension, which it views as low margin (below double-digit EBITDA).

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to double-digit EBITDA margins, and what growth is reasonable over 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets double-digit EBITDA from about two years out, driven by scaling subscale businesses (aluminium wheels, hydraulics, tractor components, air suspension). Air suspension and aluminium wheels are the near-term volume drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Where are we on raw-material and fuel price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: RM pass-through is automatic with about a one-quarter lag. Fuel-related claims are being settled with customers, with closure expected by Q3, so no major Q2/Q3 impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: When will aluminium wheels reach EBITDA and PBT breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Already EBITDA positive and at about 40,000/month breakeven. Excess older stock held back during the West Asia crisis is still landing, and PBT positive is expected from December.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed per 1 lakh aluminium wheels, and what asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR200 crores for roughly 90,000 wheels/month at an existing site. Asset turnover assumed at about INR5,000 per wheel x 90,000 x 12 per year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the industrial segment so low-margin, and what is the capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR400-450 crores FY27 capex, about INR100 crores is industrial. Windmill is double-digit margin, hydraulics low single-digit with a Q4 scale-up, and construction fabrication recovering after monsoon. Industrial is expected to reach double-digit margin in 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow negative, and will cash repay debt?
qa_highlights.answer: September sales spike raised receivables and inventory, plus about INR90 crores of Q2 capex. About INR282 crores of bill discounting and INR142 crores of WCDL were repaid from issue proceeds. Future accruals over two quarters will fund capex, not working capital.

qa_highlights.question: What are export guidance and the split between auto and industrial exports?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 exports about INR760 crores; management said full-year exports could roughly double on that base, but no formal guidance was given. Stronger export growth is expected next calendar year, with the US up 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GST refund blockage and is there a provision?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR130-140 crores of inverted-duty GST credit is stuck on the portal. Refunds are being collected via exports and inverted duty routes; no provision required, as it is a timing delay.

risks_watch: Growth slowdown from Q3 FY27 due to high GST 2.0 base and inflation; tractor demand weakness from poor monsoon in several states.
Aluminium wheel ramp-up execution: 130,000/month by March 2027 and PBT positive from December depend on clearing older stock and volume ramp-up.
Negative H1 operating cash flow and about INR130-140 crores of GST credit stuck in the portal, which delays cash.
Tariff and duty volatility on US exports; management said duties keep changing and refunds are delayed.
Industrial segment margin (about 3%) must recover to meet targets; hydraulics and fabrication timelines are back-end loaded to Q3-Q4.
